1	# ML Infrastructure Architecture Dataset
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	This dataset describes a complete machine learning infrastructure architecture as a directed graph of system components (nodes) and data/control flows (edges). It covers the full ML lifecycle from data ingestion through model serving and operational monitoring, including cross-cutting concerns like data lineage and version control.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### ml_architecture
     9	A graph structure with two arrays: `nodes` and `edges`.
    10	
    11	**Nodes** (9 total):
    12	- `id` (string): unique identifier for the component
    13	- `label` (string): display name, may include sub-labels for technology stack
    14	- `layer` (string): architectural layer — one of data, compute, serving, observability, cross-cutting
    15	- `sub_components` (array of strings): specific technologies or sub-systems within the node
    16	- `criticality` (integer, 1–10): operational criticality score
    17	- `category` (string): visual grouping category — data-layer, compute-layer, serving-layer, observability-layer
    18	
    19	**Edges** (15 total):
    20	- `source` / `target` (string): node IDs
    21	- `flow_type` (string): one of primary, feedback, lineage
    22	- `throughput_gbps` (float): data throughput in gigabits per second, range 0.1–12.5
    23	- `label` (string): short description of what flows along the edge
    24	
    25	## Data Notes
    26	- Throughput values are representative estimates for a mid-scale ML platform
    27	- Criticality scores are subjective team assessments
    28	- The graph contains cycles via feedback edges (monitoring → data platform, monitoring → training cluster)

     6	
     7	# Data Visualization Skill
     8	
     9	Chart selection guidance, Python visualization code patterns, design principles, and accessibility considerations for creating effective data visualizations.
    10	
    11	## Chart Selection Guide
    12	
    13	### Choose by Data Relationship
    14	
    15	| What You're Showing | Best Chart | Alternatives |
    16	|---|---|---|
    17	| **Trend over time** | Line chart | Area chart (if showing cumulative or composition) |
    18	| **Comparison across categories** | Vertical bar chart | Horizontal bar (many categories), lollipop chart |
    19	| **Ranking** | Horizontal bar chart | Dot plot, slope chart (comparing two periods) |
    20	| **Part-to-whole composition** | Stacked bar chart | Treemap (hierarchical), waffle chart |
    21	| **Composition over time** | Stacked area chart | 100% stacked bar (for proportion focus) |
    22	| **Distribution** | Histogram | Box plot (comparing groups), violin plot, strip plot |
    23	| **Correlation (2 variables)** | Scatter plot | Bubble chart (add 3rd variable as size) |
    24	| **Correlation (many variables)** | Heatmap (correlation matrix) | Pair plot |
    25	| **Geographic patterns** | Choropleth map | Bubble map, hex map |
    26	| **Flow / process** | Sankey diagram | Funnel chart (sequential stages) |
    27	| **Relationship network** | Network graph | Chord diagram |
    28	| **Performance vs. target** | Bullet chart | Gauge (single KPI only) |
    29	| **Multiple KPIs at once** | Small multiples | Dashboard with separate charts |
    30	
    31	### When NOT to Use Certain Charts
    32	
    33	- **Pie charts**: Avoid unless <6 categories and exact proportions matter less than rough comparison. Humans are bad at comparing angles. Use bar charts instead.
    34	- **3D charts**: Never. They distort perception and add no information.
    35	- **Dual-axis charts**: Use cautiously. They can mislead by implying correlation. Clearly label both axes if used.
    36	- **Stacked bar (many categories)**: Hard to compare middle segments. Use small multiples or grouped bars instead.
    37	- **Donut charts**: Slightly better than pie charts but same fundamental issues. Use for single KPI display at most.
    38	
    39	## Python Visualization Code Patterns
    40	
    41	### Setup and Style
    42	
    43	```python

    45	import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
    46	import seaborn as sns
    47	import pandas as pd
    48	import numpy as np

    50	# Professional style setup
    51	plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
    52	plt.rcParams.update({
    53	    'figure.figsize': (10, 6),
    54	    'figure.dpi': 150,
    55	    'font.size': 11,
    56	    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    57	    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    58	    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    59	    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    60	    'ytick.labelsize': 10,
    61	    'legend.fontsize': 10,
    62	    'figure.titlesize': 16,
    63	})
    64

    67	PALETTE_SEQUENTIAL = 'YlOrRd'

   189	### Number Formatting Helpers

   192	def format_number(val, format_type='number'):
   193	    """Format numbers for chart labels."""
   194	    if format_type == 'currency':
   195	        if abs(val) >= 1e9:
   196	            return f'${val/1e9:.1f}B'
   197	        elif abs(val) >= 1e6:
   198	            return f'${val/1e6:.1f}M'
   199	        elif abs(val) >= 1e3:
   200	            return f'${val/1e3:.1f}K'
   201	        else:
   202	            return f'${val:,.0f}'
   203	    elif format_type == 'percent':
   204	        return f'{val:.1f}%'
   205	    elif format_type == 'number':
   206	        if abs(val) >= 1e9:
   207	            return f'{val/1e9:.1f}B'
   208	        elif abs(val) >= 1e6:
   209	            return f'{val/1e6:.1f}M'
   210	        elif abs(val) >= 1e3:
   211	            return f'{val/1e3:.1f}K'

   241	## Design Principles
   242	
   243	### Color
   244	
   245	- **Use color purposefully**: Color should encode data, not decorate
   246	- **Highlight the story**: Use a bright accent color for the key insight; grey everything else
   247	- **Sequential data**: Use a single-hue gradient (light to dark) for ordered values
   248	- **Diverging data**: Use a two-hue gradient with neutral midpoint for data with a meaningful center
   249	- **Categorical data**: Use distinct hues, maximum 6-8 before it gets confusing
   250	- **Avoid red/green only**: 8% of men are red-green colorblind. Use blue/orange as primary pair
   251	
   252	### Typography
   253	
   254	- **Title states the insight**: "Revenue grew 23% YoY" beats "Revenue by Month"
   255	- **Subtitle adds context**: Date range, filters applied, data source
   256	- **Axis labels are readable**: Never rotated 90 degrees if avoidable. Shorten or wrap instead
   257	- **Data labels add precision**: Use on key points, not every single bar
   258	- **Annotation highlights**: Call out specific points with text annotations
   259	
   260	### Layout
   261	
   262	- **Reduce chart junk**: Remove gridlines, borders, backgrounds that don't carry information
   263	- **Sort meaningfully**: Categories sorted by value (not alphabetically) unless there's a natural order (months, stages)
   264	- **Appropriate aspect ratio**: Time series wider than tall (3:1 to 2:1); comparisons can be squarer
   265	- **White space is good**: Don't cram charts together. Give each visualization room to breathe
   266	
   267	### Accuracy
   268	
   269	- **Bar charts start at zero**: Always. A bar from 95 to 100 exaggerates a 5% difference
   270	- **Line charts can have non-zero baselines**: When the range of variation is meaningful
   271	- **Consistent scales across panels**: When comparing multiple charts, use the same axis range
   272	- **Show uncertainty**: Error bars, confidence intervals, or ranges when data is uncertain
   273	- **Label your axes**: Never make the reader guess what the numbers mean
   274	
   275	## Accessibility Considerations
   276	
   277	### Color Blindness
   278	
   279	- Never rely on color alone to distinguish data series
   280	- Add pattern fills, different line styles (solid, dashed, dotted), or direct labels
   281	- Test with a colorblind simulator (e.g., Coblis, Sim Daltonism)
   282	- Use the colorblind-friendly palette: `sns.color_palette("colorblind")`
   283	
   284	### Screen Readers
   285	
   286	- Include alt text describing the chart's key finding
   287	- Provide a data table alternative alongside the visualization
   288	- Use semantic titles and labels
   289	
   290	### General Accessibility

import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch, FancyArrowPatch
import numpy as np

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

nodes = {n['id']: n for n in data['ml_architecture']['nodes']}
edges = data['ml_architecture']['edges']

# Dark theme setup
plt.style.use('dark_background')
plt.rcParams.update({
    'figure.facecolor': '#1a1a2e',
    'axes.facecolor': '#1a1a2e',
    'axes.edgecolor': '#444444',
    'axes.labelcolor': '#cccccc',
    'text.color': '#eeeeee',
    'xtick.color': '#aaaaaa',
    'ytick.color': '#aaaaaa',
    'grid.color': '#333333',
    'figure.dpi': 200,
    'font.size': 10,
    'axes.titlesize': 16,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
})

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 12))
ax.set_facecolor('#1a1a2e')

# Color mapping by category
category_colors = {
    'data-layer': '#4C8BF5',      # blue
    'compute-layer': '#4CAF50',   # green
    'serving-layer': '#FF9800',   # orange
    'observability-layer': '#F44336',  # red
}

# Node positions - pipeline layout with stages from left to right
positions = {
    'data_platform': (1.5, 6),
    'feature_store': (4.5, 6),
    'training_cluster': (7.5, 6),
    'model_registry': (10.5, 6),
    'inference_online': (13.5, 7.5),
    'inference_offline': (13.5, 4.5),
    'ab_experiment': (16.5, 6),
    'monitoring': (19.5, 6),
    'version_control': (7.5, 2.0),
}

# Draw edges first (so they appear behind nodes)
for edge in edges:
    src = edge['source']
    tgt = edge['target']
    flow_type = edge['flow_type']
    throughput = edge['throughput_gbps']
    label = edge.get('label', '')
    
    x1, y1 = positions[src]
    x2, y2 = positions[tgt]
    
    # Edge styling
    if flow_type == 'primary':
        color = '#88aaff'
        linestyle = '-'
        alpha = 0.75
        linewidth = max(1.5, throughput * 0.6)
        zorder = 1
    elif flow_type == 'feedback':
        color = '#ff6b6b'
        linestyle = '-'
        alpha = 0.85
        linewidth = max(1.5, throughput * 1.5)
        zorder = 3
    else:  # lineage
        color = '#bb86fc'
        linestyle = '--'
        alpha = 0.6
        linewidth = max(1.0, throughput * 2.5)
        zorder = 1
    
    # Special routing for feedback edges (curved arcs going backward/up)
    if flow_type == 'feedback':
        if src == 'monitoring' and tgt == 'data_platform':
            # Large arc over the top
            mid_x = (x1 + x2) / 2
            mid_y = max(y1, y2) + 4.5
            t = np.linspace(0, 1, 100)
            # Quadratic bezier
            x_path = (1-t)**2 * x1 + 2*(1-t)*t * mid_x + t**2 * x2
            y_path = (1-t)**2 * y1 + 2*(1-t)*t * mid_y + t**2 * y2
            ax.plot(x_path, y_path, color=color, linewidth=linewidth, alpha=alpha, linestyle=linestyle, zorder=zorder)
            # Arrow at the end
            arrow_idx = -5
            ax.annotate('', xy=(x_path[arrow_idx], y_path[arrow_idx]),
                        xytext=(x_path[arrow_idx-1], y_path[arrow_idx-1]),
                        arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color, lw=linewidth*0.8))
            # Label
            ax.text(mid_x, mid_y + 0.3, label, fontsize=8, color='#ff9999',
                    ha='center', va='bottom', fontweight='bold')
            continue
        elif src == 'monitoring' and tgt == 'training_cluster':
            # Arc from monitoring back to training cluster
            mid_x = (x1 + x2) / 2
            mid_y = max(y1, y2) + 3.0
            t = np.linspace(0, 1, 100)
            x_path = (1-t)**2 * x1 + 2*(1-t)*t * mid_x + t**2 * x2
            y_path = (1-t)**2 * y1 + 2*(1-t)*t * mid_y + t**2 * y2
            ax.plot(x_path, y_path, color=color, linewidth=linewidth, alpha=alpha, linestyle=linestyle, zorder=zorder)
            arrow_idx = -5
            ax.annotate('', xy=(x_path[arrow_idx], y_path[arrow_idx]),
                        xytext=(x_path[arrow_idx-1], y_path[arrow_idx-1]),
                        arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color, lw=linewidth*0.8))
            ax.text(mid_x + 1.5, mid_y + 0.2, label, fontsize=8, color='#ff9999',
                    ha='center', va='bottom', fontweight='bold')
            continue
    
    # Special routing for lineage edges from version_control
    if flow_type == 'lineage':
        if src == 'version_control' and tgt == 'feature_store':
            # Up-left diagonal
            pass
        elif src == 'version_control' and tgt == 'training_cluster':
            pass
        elif src == 'version_control' and tgt == 'model_registry':
            pass
        elif src == 'data_platform' and tgt == 'version_control':
            pass
    
    # Standard straight-line edges with slight curvature for branching
    if src == 'model_registry' and tgt in ('inference_online', 'inference_offline'):
        # Branching edges
        mid_x = (x1 + x2) / 2
        mid_y = (y1 + y2) / 2
        t = np.linspace(0, 1, 50)
        x_path = (1-t)*x1 + t*x2
        y_path = (1-t)*y1 + t*y2
        ax.plot(x_path, y_path, color=color, linewidth=linewidth, alpha=alpha, linestyle=linestyle, zorder=zorder)
        # Arrow
        arrow_idx = -3
        ax.annotate('', xy=(x_path[arrow_idx], y_path[arrow_idx]),
                    xytext=(x_path[arrow_idx-1], y_path[arrow_idx-1]),
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color, lw=linewidth*0.8))
        # Label near middle
        ax.text(mid_x + 0.3, mid_y + (0.4 if tgt == 'inference_online' else -0.4),
                f"{label}\n({throughput} Gbps)", fontsize=7, color='#aaccff',
                ha='center', va='bottom' if tgt == 'inference_online' else 'top')
        continue
    elif src in ('inference_online', 'inference_offline') and tgt == 'ab_experiment':
        # Converging edges
        mid_x = (x1 + x2) / 2
        mid_y = (y1 + y2) / 2
        t = np.linspace(0, 1, 50)
        x_path = (1-t)*x1 + t*x2
        y_path = (1-t)*y1 + t*y2
        ax.plot(x_path, y_path, color=color, linewidth=linewidth, alpha=alpha, linestyle=linestyle, zorder=zorder)
        arrow_idx = -3
        ax.annotate('', xy=(x_path[arrow_idx], y_path[arrow_idx]),
                    xytext=(x_path[arrow_idx-1], y_path[arrow_idx-1]),
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color, lw=linewidth*0.8))
        ax.text(mid_x - 0.2, mid_y + (0.3 if src == 'inference_online' else -0.3),
                f"{label}\n({throughput} Gbps)", fontsize=7, color='#aaccff',
                ha='center', va='bottom' if src == 'inference_online' else 'top')
        continue
    
    # Default straight edge
    dx = x2 - x1
    dy = y2 - y1
    dist = np.sqrt(dx**2 + dy**2)
    
    # Shorten slightly so arrow doesn't overlap node
    shrink = 0.35
    x1_adj = x1 + (dx/dist) * shrink if dist > 0 else x1
    y1_adj = y1 + (dy/dist) * shrink if dist > 0 else y1
    x2_adj = x2 - (dx/dist) * shrink if dist > 0 else x2
    y2_adj = y2 - (dy/dist) * shrink if dist > 0 else y2
    
    ax.annotate('', xy=(x2_adj, y2_adj), xytext=(x1_adj, y1_adj),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color, lw=linewidth,
                                linestyle=linestyle, alpha=alpha,
                                connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0.05' if flow_type == 'lineage' else 'arc3,rad=0'))
    
    # Edge labels for primary non-branching edges
    if flow_type == 'primary':
        mid_x = (x1 + x2) / 2
        mid_y = (y1 + y2) / 2
        ax.text(mid_x, mid_y + 0.25, f"{label}", fontsize=7, color='#aaccff',
                ha='center', va='bottom', fontweight='medium')
        ax.text(mid_x, mid_y - 0.15, f"{throughput} Gbps", fontsize=6, color='#88aaff',
                ha='center', va='top', style='italic')
    elif flow_type == 'lineage':
        mid_x = (x1 + x2) / 2
        mid_y = (y1 + y2) / 2
        offset = 0.25
        ax.text(mid_x + offset, mid_y + offset, label, fontsize=7, color='#d4aaff',
                ha='center', va='bottom', style='italic')

# Draw nodes
for node_id, node in nodes.items():
    x, y = positions[node_id]
    color = category_colors.get(node['category'], '#888888')
    criticality = node['criticality']
    
    # Node size by criticality (radius)
    radius = 0.5 + (criticality / 10) * 0.5
    
    # Draw node as rounded rectangle
    box_width = 2.2
    box_height = 1.4
    
    # Glow effect
    glow = FancyBboxPatch((x - box_width/2 - 0.05, y - box_height/2 - 0.05),
                          box_width + 0.1, box_height + 0.1,
                          boxstyle="round,pad=0.15",
                          facecolor=color, alpha=0.15,
                          edgecolor='none', zorder=4)
    ax.add_patch(glow)
    
    # Main node box
    box = FancyBboxPatch((x - box_width/2, y - box_height/2),
                         box_width, box_height,
                         boxstyle="round,pad=0.12",
                         facecolor='#16213e', alpha=0.95,
                         edgecolor=color, linewidth=2.5, zorder=5)
    ax.add_patch(box)
    
    # Criticality indicator - small circle with score
    crit_circle = plt.Circle((x + box_width/2 - 0.2, y + box_height/2 - 0.2),
                              0.22, facecolor=color, edgecolor='white',
                              linewidth=1, alpha=0.9, zorder=6)
    ax.add_patch(crit_circle)
    ax.text(x + box_width/2 - 0.2, y + box_height/2 - 0.2, str(criticality),
            fontsize=8, color='white', ha='center', va='center',
            fontweight='bold', zorder=7)
    
    # Node label
    label_text = node['label'].replace('\n', '\n')
    ax.text(x, y + 0.05, label_text, fontsize=9, color='white',
            ha='center', va='center', fontweight='bold', zorder=7,
            linespacing=1.1)
    
    # Sub-components as smaller text below
    sub_text = '  |  '.join(node['sub_components'][:2])
    if len(node['sub_components']) > 2:
        sub_text += '  |  ...'
    ax.text(x, y - box_height/2 - 0.25, sub_text, fontsize=6.5, color='#aaaaaa',
            ha='center', va='top', zorder=7, style='italic')

# Stage labels at the bottom
stage_labels = [
    (1.5, 'DATA LAYER'),
    (4.5, 'DATA LAYER'),
    (7.5, 'COMPUTE LAYER'),
    (10.5, 'COMPUTE LAYER'),
    (13.5, 'SERVING LAYER'),
    (16.5, 'SERVING LAYER'),
    (19.5, 'OBSERVABILITY'),
]
for x, label in stage_labels:
    ax.text(x, 0.6, label, fontsize=8, color='#666666',
            ha='center', va='center', fontweight='bold',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#0f0f23', edgecolor='#333333', alpha=0.8))

# Legend
legend_elements = [
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#16213e', edgecolor='#4C8BF5', linewidth=2, label='Data Layer'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#16213e', edgecolor='#4CAF50', linewidth=2, label='Compute Layer'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#16213e', edgecolor='#FF9800', linewidth=2, label='Serving Layer'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#16213e', edgecolor='#F44336', linewidth=2, label='Observability Layer'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], color='#88aaff', linewidth=2, linestyle='-', label='Primary Data Flow'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], color='#bb86fc', linewidth=2, linestyle='--', label='Data Lineage / Version Control'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], color='#ff6b6b', linewidth=2, linestyle='-', label='Feedback Loop'),
]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper center',
          bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.02), ncol=4, fontsize=9,
          frameon=True, facecolor='#1a1a2e', edgecolor='#444444',
          labelcolor='white')

# Title and subtitle
ax.set_title('ML Infrastructure Pipeline Architecture', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold',
             color='white', pad=20)
ax.text(10.5, 10.5, 'End-to-end flow: Data Platform → Feature Store → Training → Registry → Inference → A/B Testing → Monitoring',
        fontsize=11, color='#aaaaaa', ha='center', va='center', style='italic')

# Online/offline branching annotation
ax.annotate('Online / Offline\nBranching', xy=(13.5, 6.2), xytext=(13.5, 9.0),
            fontsize=9, color='#FF9800', ha='center', va='bottom',
            fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#FF9800', lw=1.5),
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#1a1a2e', edgecolor='#FF9800', alpha=0.9))

# Feedback loop annotation
ax.annotate('Closed-loop MLOps\nFeedback', xy=(17.5, 8.5), xytext=(17.5, 10.0),
            fontsize=9, color='#F44336', ha='center', va='bottom',
            fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#F44336', lw=1.5),
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#1a1a2e', edgecolor='#F44336', alpha=0.9))

# Data lineage annotation
ax.annotate('Cross-cutting Data Lineage\n& Version Control', xy=(7.5, 2.7), xytext=(4.0, 1.0),
            fontsize=9, color='#bb86fc', ha='center', va='top',
            fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#bb86fc', lw=1.5, connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0.2'),
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#1a1a2e', edgecolor='#bb86fc', alpha=0.9))

# Axis setup
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 21.5)
ax.set_ylim(-0.5, 11.0)
ax.set_aspect('equal')
ax.axis('off')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=200, bbox_inches='tight',
            facecolor='#1a1a2e', edgecolor='none')
plt.close()
print("Saved /app/output/result.png")
